Aggregate CTAS site scores into a gsm-shaped CTAS summary

Summarize_CTAS.Rd

Pivots the long CTAS results frame (one row per site x timeseries x feature) into the gsm reporting dfResults contract (one row per site x synthetic MetricID) so the stock gsm.kri report can render it unchanged. Each parameter_category_2 (data field, e.g. "AST", "SYSBP") becomes its own MetricID (ctas_<field>); metric families are collapsed with max(Score) so a field scored by both range_normalized and ratio_missing shows as one CTAS row. When bByFeature = TRUE, one MetricID per (field x CTAS feature) is emitted instead.

Usage

Summarize_CTAS(
  dfResults,
  dfSubjects,
  bIncludeMissingness = TRUE,
  bByFeature = FALSE,
  strStudyID = NULL,
  dSnapshotDate = Sys.Date()
)

Arguments

dfResults

data.frame Stacked CTAS results, typically Reporting_Results$results from the reporting Results workflow. Must contain study, site, parameter_category_2, parameter_category_3, feature, fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp, timeseries_id.

dfSubjects

data.frame Standardised subjects with studyid, subject_id, site. Used to complete the (study x site x MetricID) grid so sites with no scored timeseries stay visible.

bIncludeMissingness

logical Include the ratio_missing metric family (parameter_category_3 == "ratio_missing") in the aggregation. Default TRUE.

bByFeature

logical Group by (data field x CTAS feature) instead of by data field only. Default FALSE.

strStudyID

character Optional single StudyID used for every row (overrides per-row study). Default NULL -> use the study column.

dSnapshotDate

Date Snapshot date stamped on every row. Default Sys.Date().

Value

data.frame with the gsm reporting dfResults columns (MetricID, GroupID, GroupLevel, StudyID, SnapshotDate, Score) plus the CTAS grouping keys (parameter_category_2, and feature when bByFeature = TRUE) so downstream steps can label metrics without a re-join.

Details

The Score is the max fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp across every contributing (timeseries x feature) row in the group. Sites present in dfSubjects but absent from dfResults (e.g. no scorable timeseries for a field) are retained with Score = NA so the CTAS overview table cannot silently drop them.

Flag is intentionally not emitted here – run Flag_CTAS() on the returned frame to add it. Splitting Summarize + Flag mirrors the gsm.core::Summarize() / gsm.core::Flag() seam so users can swap thresholds without re-aggregating.

See also

Flag_CTAS() to add the Flag column.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
lReporting <- workr::RunWorkflows(
  lReportingWorkflows["Results"],
  lData = c(lMapped, list(lAnalyzed = lAnalysis))
)
dfSummary <- Summarize_CTAS(
  dfResults = lReporting$Reporting_Results$results,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects
)
} # }
